The invention relates to a watch-type mobile terminal configured to allow a user to conveniently search and use payment-related items, such as payment cards, coupons, membership cards, and other payment or benefit information.

The watch-type mobile terminal includes a display unit, a sensing unit, and a control unit. The display unit is configured to display payment information on a screen. The payment information may include, for example, one or more payment cards, coupons, membership cards, reward cards, discount information, or other items associated with payment or user benefits. The sensing unit is configured to sense a user input applied to the terminal, including a touch input applied to the display unit. The control unit is configured to control the display unit and the sensing unit, and to process user inputs related to the displayed payment information.

In operation, the control unit detects a first input signal related to the payment information displayed on the screen. The first input signal may be a touch input applied to at least a portion of the displayed payment information. In particular, the first input signal may correspond to a touch input in which a touched area or a touch pressure exceeds a predetermined value. Accordingly, the terminal may distinguish an intentional input for searching or selecting payment-related information from a general or accidental touch.

When the first input signal is detected, the control unit may display an indicator associated with the payment information or may display an item included in the payment information. The indicator may guide the user to available payment-related items or may visually identify a particular item, such as a payment card, coupon, or membership card. In response to a second input signal, the control unit may enlarge the displayed item. For example, when the user applies an additional touch input, drag input, long press, or other predetermined gesture, the control unit may enlarge the selected item on the display unit so that the user can more easily view, identify, or use the item.

As a result, the watch-type mobile terminal enables a user to quickly search payment-related items on a small display screen and conveniently access a desired card, coupon, membership card, or similar item.
outputs.L4:
A watch-type mobile terminal and a method for controlling the same are provided to improve the convenience of searching for and using payment-related items. The watch-type mobile terminal includes a display unit, a sensing unit configured to detect touch inputs applied to the display unit or to the body of the terminal, and a controller configured to control the display unit based on the detected touch inputs. The payment-related items may include, for example, credit cards, debit cards, transportation cards, coupons, vouchers, membership cards, reward cards, and other items that can be used during a payment process.

When a user applies a touch input having a predetermined characteristic, the controller may determine that the user intends to access a payment function. For instance, if the sensing unit detects a touch input having a pressure level greater than a reference value, or a touch input having a contact area greater than a reference area, the controller may display one or more indicators associated with payment-related items. These indicators may allow the user to quickly recognize available cards, coupons, memberships, or other payment benefits without having to enter a separate payment application or perform multiple menu navigation steps.

In one implementation, the display unit may initially display a watch screen, a home screen, or another general screen. When a strong touch, a wide-area touch, or another predefined touch input is detected, the controller may switch the displayed screen to a payment item selection screen. The payment item selection screen may include a list, icons, tabs, or graphical indicators representing payment-related items stored in the terminal or accessible through a connected external device or server. The controller may arrange the payment-related items according to a usage frequency, a current location, a store type, an expiration date, a discount rate, or a user preference.

The user may select one of the displayed payment-related items by applying a second touch input. In response to the second touch input, the controller may enlarge the selected item or display detailed information related to the selected item. For example, when the user selects a particular card, coupon, or membership, the corresponding barcode, QR code, card image, authentication screen, or payment information may be enlarged on the display unit. By enlarging the selected item, the terminal allows a store clerk, payment terminal, or scanner to more easily recognize the item during a payment transaction.

The control method may include detecting, by the sensing unit, a first touch input applied to the watch-type mobile terminal, determining whether the first touch input satisfies a predetermined condition relating to pressure, contact area, duration, or touch pattern, and displaying payment-related indicators or payment items when the predetermined condition is satisfied. The method may further include detecting a second touch input applied to one of the displayed indicators or payment items, selecting a payment-related item corresponding to the second touch input, and enlarging or otherwise emphasizing the selected item on the display unit.

Accordingly, the watch-type mobile terminal enables a user to quickly access cards, coupons, memberships, and other payment-related items using intuitive touch operations. Because the terminal can display relevant payment items in response to a strong or large-area touch and can enlarge a selected item through an additional input, the user can conveniently search for and present payment information even on the relatively small display of a wearable device. This improves usability, reduces the number of input steps required during payment, and enhances the overall payment experience.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and simple, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, things, or ideas. For example, when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book, not just any book.

“The” gives clarity to communication. It points the listener or reader toward something known or already mentioned. Without it, sentences can sound unclear or incomplete. Compare “I saw dog” with “I saw the dog.” The second sentence is much more natural and specific.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” appears everywhere: in stories, conversations, news articles, songs, and speeches. It helps shape meaning and makes language more precise. This small word proves that even the simplest parts of language can have a powerful role.

## Invention Disclosure: Gesture-Adaptive Smartwatch Payment Interface with Searchable Cards and Coupons

### Title  
**Smartwatch Payment Interface for Contextual Searching, Selection, and Gesture-Based Enlargement of Payment Cards and Coupons**

### Field of the Invention  
The present invention relates generally to wearable electronic devices and, more particularly, to a smartwatch-based payment interface configured to search and present payment cards, loyalty cards, tickets, vouchers, and coupons during a payment transaction, and to enlarge selected interface items in response to user touch gestures.

### Background  
Smartwatches and other wearable devices are increasingly used for contactless payments. However, due to limited display size, users may experience difficulty locating a desired payment card, loyalty card, discount coupon, or other transaction-related credential at the time of purchase. Existing wallet applications typically present cards in a static list or carousel, requiring repeated swiping or scrolling. Such interaction may be inconvenient during checkout, particularly when the user is under time pressure.

Additionally, coupons and loyalty benefits may be stored separately from payment cards or may not be surfaced at the appropriate time. A user may therefore fail to apply an available coupon or may need to manually search through multiple screens. The limited display area of a smartwatch further makes it difficult to review card identifiers, coupon terms, barcodes, QR codes, or selectable transaction items.

Accordingly, there is a need for an improved smartwatch payment interface that permits convenient searching of payment cards and coupons during a payment session and that dynamically enlarges selected items based on touch gestures to improve usability and reduce transaction friction.

### Summary of the Invention  
Disclosed is a smartwatch payment interface that enables a user to initiate or continue a payment session while conveniently searching stored payment cards, coupons, loyalty credentials, tickets, passes, or other transaction items. The interface may present searchable transaction items based on user input, merchant context, location, purchase amount, transaction history, expiration date, reward availability, or combinations thereof.

In one embodiment, the smartwatch detects a payment context, such as activation of a wallet application, proximity to a point-of-sale terminal, receipt of a near-field communication signal, detection of a merchant beacon, or selection of a payment mode. The smartwatch then displays one or more candidate items, including payment cards and applicable coupons. A search function may be invoked by touch input, voice input, text input, gesture input, or contextual triggering. Search results may be ranked according to relevance to the current transaction.

The interface further detects user touch gestures applied to displayed cards, coupons, or other payment-related items. In response to a predefined gesture, such as a tap-and-hold, force touch, pinch-out gesture, double tap, long press, drag, or dwell gesture, the smartwatch enlarges the selected item or a selected portion of the item. Enlarged content may include a payment card face, last four digits of a card number, issuer logo, coupon code, barcode, QR code, expiration date, discount amount, merchant name, reward balance, or “use now” control.

The enlarged item may be displayed in a magnified overlay, expanded card view, zoomed carousel position, or full-screen transaction-ready presentation. In certain embodiments, the enlarged item remains active for payment, redemption, or scanning. In other embodiments, the enlarged item may be automatically reduced when the user lifts a finger, performs a reverse gesture, completes payment, or after expiration of a timeout period.

### Brief Description of the Drawings  
The following drawings may be prepared to support a patent application:

1. **FIG. 1** illustrates a smartwatch having a payment interface displaying a plurality of payment cards and coupons.  
2. **FIG. 2** illustrates a search interface for locating transaction items during a payment session.  
3. **FIG. 3** illustrates a gesture-based enlargement of a selected payment card.  
4. **FIG. 4** illustrates enlargement of a coupon including a machine-readable code.  
5. **FIG. 5** illustrates a flow diagram for contextual searching and gesture-responsive enlargement.  
6. **FIG. 6** illustrates a system including a smartwatch, a mobile device, a payment server, a coupon server, and a merchant point-of-sale terminal.

### Detailed Description  

#### System Overview  
In one embodiment, a wearable electronic device, such as a smartwatch, includes a display, a touch-sensitive input surface, one or more processors, memory, a wireless communication interface, and a payment module. The payment module may include a near-field communication transceiver, secure element, trusted execution environment, tokenization module, or other secure payment component.

The smartwatch stores or accesses a plurality of transaction items. The transaction items may include payment cards, debit cards, credit cards, prepaid cards, transit cards, loyalty cards, reward accounts, coupons, vouchers, discounts, merchant offers, gift cards, tickets, passes, receipts, or digital credentials. The transaction items may be stored locally on the smartwatch, synchronized from a companion mobile device, or retrieved from a remote server.

The smartwatch executes a payment interface configured to display transaction items in a searchable and gesture-adaptive manner. The interface is particularly adapted for small-screen wearable devices by prioritizing relevant items and enlarging user-selected items in response to touch gestures.

#### Payment Context Detection  
The smartwatch may determine that a payment context exists by detecting one or more payment-related conditions. Such conditions may include:

- user activation of a wallet application;
- double pressing a physical button;
- proximity to an NFC point-of-sale terminal;
- detection of a merchant wireless beacon;
- receipt of transaction information from a merchant terminal;
- detection of a known merchant location;
- calendar or ticket context;
- geolocation near a store;
- recognition of a recurring transaction pattern;
- scanning of a merchant code;
- selection of a payment complication or shortcut.

Upon detecting the payment context, the smartwatch may automatically present a payment interface including candidate payment cards and coupons relevant to the context.

#### Searchable Cards and Coupons  
The payment interface includes a search function permitting convenient retrieval of stored cards, coupons, and related transaction items during payment. The search function may be presented as a search icon, search field, voice input prompt, gesture-activated search mode, or automatically generated result list.

Search input may include:

- typed characters entered using an on-screen keyboard;
- handwriting input;
- voice input;
- dictation;
- selection of merchant category;
- scrolling or rotating a crown input;
- tapping suggested filters;
- drawing a gesture associated with a stored item;
- contextual input derived from merchant identity or transaction amount.

In response to the search input, the smartwatch identifies matching transaction items. For example, a user may search “coffee,” and the interface may display a stored coffee shop loyalty card, a coupon for the coffee shop, and a preferred credit card offering increased rewards for dining purchases. A user may search “Visa,” and the interface may show Visa payment cards and coupons associated with Visa offers.

Search results may be ranked based on one or more relevance factors, including merchant identity, location, time of day, transaction amount, expiration date, coupon value, prior usage, card reward rate, default payment preference, frequency of use, payment success history, or user-selected favorites.

#### Coupon Association with Payment Cards  
In some embodiments, coupons are automatically associated with payment cards or merchants. When a user selects a payment card, the smartwatch may display coupons applicable to the selected card, merchant, or transaction. Conversely, when a coupon is selected, the smartwatch may recommend one or more compatible payment cards.

For example, the interface may display a payment card tile with one or more coupon badges indicating available discounts. A coupon badge may be selectable, expandable, or automatically applied during payment. The smartwatch may notify the user when a coupon is about to expire or when a selected payment card qualifies for an offer.

#### Gesture-Based Enlargement  
The smartwatch detects touch gestures applied to displayed transaction items. A transaction item may be enlarged when the user performs a predetermined gesture on the item. The gesture may include, without limitation:

- tap-and-hold;
- long press;
- double tap;
- pinch-out;
- drag toward a center region;
- force press;
- dwell of a fingertip over an item;
- rotational input while touching an item;
- swipe-and-hold;
- press on a coupon badge;
- two-finger expansion gesture.

In response to the gesture, the selected item is enlarged relative to other displayed items. The enlargement may occur by scaling the item, expanding the item into a full-screen view, displaying a magnification window, increasing text size, increasing code size, or enlarging a selected portion of the item.

For example, when a payment card is enlarged, the interface may show the card issuer, card art, last four digits, default status, available balance, reward rate, and a payment activation control. When a coupon is enlarged, the interface may show the merchant name, discount amount, expiration date, coupon terms, redemption button, barcode, QR code, or numeric coupon code.

The enlarged item may remain selected for transaction processing. Thus, a user may enlarge a coupon to permit scanning by a cashier and then return to the associated payment card for NFC payment. Alternatively, the enlarged coupon may be transmitted electronically to the merchant terminal.

#### Dynamic Layout During Enlargement  
When an item is enlarged, non-selected items may be reduced, dimmed, moved to an edge, partially hidden, stacked, or placed in a background layer. The enlarged item may occupy a central display region. In one embodiment, a selected item is enlarged proportionally according to gesture magnitude. For example, a greater pinch-out distance produces a larger view of the item.

The interface may support progressive enlargement. A first gesture level may enlarge the item to a preview state, while a second gesture level may enlarge the item to a transaction state. A third gesture level may activate the item for payment or redemption.

The interface may also enlarge only the portion of the item nearest the touch location. For instance, touching a coupon expiration date may enlarge the date, while touching a barcode region may enlarge the barcode. Touching a card identifier may enlarge the last four digits or card nickname.

#### Payment and Redemption Flow  
A representative payment flow may include the following steps:

1. A smartwatch detects a payment context.  
2. The smartwatch displays a plurality of transaction items including payment cards and coupons.  
3. The smartwatch receives search input from the user or contextual information from a merchant.  
4. The smartwatch identifies and ranks cards and coupons relevant to the search input or context.  
5. The smartwatch displays the ranked items on the smartwatch display.  
6. The user touches a desired item and performs an enlargement gesture.  
7. The smartwatch enlarges the selected card or coupon.  
8. The user confirms selection of the enlarged item.  
9. The smartwatch applies a coupon, displays a scannable code, transmits coupon data, activates a selected payment card, or performs a contactless payment transaction.  
10. The smartwatch returns to a compact interface or presents a transaction confirmation.

#### Security and Privacy  
The smartwatch may require authentication before displaying sensitive payment information or before initiating payment. Authentication may include wrist detection, biometric verification, passcode entry, proximity to a paired mobile device, or prior unlocking. Sensitive card information may be masked, tokenized, or stored in a secure element. Coupon information may be displayed without revealing payment credentials.

In some embodiments, the enlargement of sensitive details is permitted only after authentication. For example, a card may be visually enlarged before authentication, but payment activation controls or card details may remain hidden until authentication is completed.

#### Machine Learning and Personalization  
The search and ranking function may be personalized using historical usage patterns. The smartwatch or associated server may learn which cards or coupons a user prefers at certain merchants, locations, times, or transaction categories. The interface may automatically elevate frequently used cards or high-value coupons in the payment interface.

The system may also infer that a coupon is relevant based on merchant category or past redemption patterns. For example, if the user frequently uses a grocery rewards card at a grocery store, the smartwatch may automatically present that rewards card and available grocery coupons when the user enters the store.

### Example Use Cases  

#### Example 1: Merchant-Specific Coupon Search  
A user enters a coffee shop and double presses a smartwatch button to open the wallet. The smartwatch detects the merchant location and displays a preferred payment card, a loyalty card, and two available coupons. The user taps and holds a coupon. The coupon expands to show a QR code and expiration date. The cashier scans the enlarged QR code, and the user then pays using the selected card.

#### Example 2: Search During Checkout  
At a department store, a user opens the smartwatch wallet and speaks “department coupon.” The smartwatch searches stored coupons and payment offers, then displays a ranked list of coupons and cards. The user performs a pinch-out gesture on a coupon tile. The tile enlarges to full-screen view with a barcode. After coupon redemption, the user swipes to the recommended payment card and completes payment.

#### Example 3: Card Enlargement for Selection Confidence  
A user has multiple cards with similar appearances. During payment, the smartwatch displays cards in a compact carousel. The user long presses a card. The card enlarges and displays the issuer name, nickname, and last four digits. The user confirms that it is the desired card and performs NFC payment.

### Advantages  
The disclosed invention provides several advantages, including:

- improved usability of payment interfaces on small smartwatch displays;
- faster access to desired payment cards and coupons during checkout;
- contextual ranking of relevant transaction items;
- reduced need for repeated scrolling through wallet items;
- improved visibility of barcodes, QR codes, coupon terms, and card identifiers;
- gesture-based enlargement that preserves efficient one-handed interaction;
- integration of payment selection and coupon redemption in a unified interface;
- reduced likelihood of missing applicable discounts or rewards.

### Abstract  
A smartwatch payment interface is disclosed. The interface presents searchable payment cards, coupons, loyalty credentials, and other transaction items during a payment session. The smartwatch detects a payment context and receives search input or contextual information to identify and rank relevant transaction items. A user may select a displayed card or coupon using touch input. In response to a touch gesture, such as a long press, double tap, pinch-out, or dwell gesture, the smartwatch enlarges the selected item or a selected portion thereof. The enlarged item may display payment card information, coupon data, barcodes, QR codes, expiration information, or transaction controls. The selected item may remain active for payment or redemption while enlarged.

### Representative Claims  

#### Claim 1  
A wearable electronic device comprising:  
a display;  
a touch-sensitive input surface;  
one or more processors; and  
memory storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the wearable electronic device to:  
detect a payment context;  
display, on the display, a plurality of transaction items comprising at least one payment card and at least one coupon;  
receive search input associated with a payment transaction;  
identify, based at least in part on the search input, one or more matching transaction items from the plurality of transaction items;  
display the one or more matching transaction items on the display;  
detect a touch gesture applied to a selected transaction item of the one or more matching transaction items; and  
in response to detecting the touch gesture, enlarge the selected transaction item on the display.

#### Claim 2  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the selected transaction item comprises a coupon, and wherein enlarging the selected transaction item comprises displaying an enlarged machine-readable code associated with the coupon.

#### Claim 3  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the selected transaction item comprises a payment card, and wherein enlarging the selected transaction item comprises displaying at least one of a card issuer, card nickname, masked account identifier, reward attribute, or payment activation control.

#### Claim 4  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein detecting the payment context comprises detecting proximity to a point-of-sale terminal.

#### Claim 5  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein detecting the payment context comprises detecting at least one of activation of a wallet application, a merchant location, a merchant beacon, an NFC signal, or a user input associated with payment.

#### Claim 6  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the search input comprises voice input.

#### Claim 7  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the search input comprises touch input entered through the touch-sensitive input surface.

#### Claim 8  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the wearable electronic device to rank the one or more matching transaction items based on at least one of merchant identity, location, coupon expiration date, coupon value, card reward rate, transaction amount, user preference, or prior usage history.

#### Claim 9  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the touch gesture comprises at least one of a long press, tap-and-hold, double tap, pinch-out gesture, force touch, dwell gesture, drag gesture, or swipe-and-hold gesture.

#### Claim 10  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein enlarging the selected transaction item comprises enlarging a portion of the selected transaction item corresponding to a location of the touch gesture.

#### Claim 11  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the wearable electronic device to reduce display prominence of non-selected transaction items while the selected transaction item is enlarged.

#### Claim 12  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the selected transaction item remains active for payment or redemption while enlarged.

#### Claim 13  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the wearable electronic device to associate the at least one coupon with a compatible payment card.

#### Claim 14  
The wearable electronic device of claim 13, wherein the instructions further cause the wearable electronic device to recommend the compatible payment card in response to selection of the coupon.

#### Claim 15  
The wearable electronic device of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the wearable electronic device to authenticate a user before enabling payment using an enlarged payment card.

#### Claim 16  
A method performed by a smartwatch, the method comprising:  
detecting, by the smartwatch, initiation of a payment session;  
presenting a searchable payment interface including payment cards and coupons;  
receiving search criteria during the payment session;  
displaying cards and coupons matching the search criteria;  
detecting a user touch gesture directed to a selected card or coupon;  
enlarging the selected card or coupon in response to the user touch gesture; and  
enabling payment or redemption using the selected card or coupon.

#### Claim 17  
The method of claim 16, further comprising displaying an enlarged barcode or QR code when the selected card or coupon comprises a coupon.

#### Claim 18  
The method of claim 16, further comprising activating a contactless payment module when the selected card or coupon comprises a payment card.

#### Claim 19  
The method of claim 16, further comprising automatically displaying coupons applicable to a merchant associated with the payment session.

#### Claim 20  
A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors of a smartwatch, cause the smartwatch to:  
display a plurality of payment-related items including payment cards and coupons;  
search the plurality of payment-related items based on user input or transaction context;  
present matching payment-related items on a smartwatch display;  
detect a touch gesture corresponding to one of the matching payment-related items; and  
enlarge the corresponding payment-related item on the smartwatch display for selection, payment, or redemption.

본 발명은 시계형 이동 단말기 및 그 제어방법에 관한 것이다. 본 발명의 일 실시예에 따른 시계형 이동 단말기는, 결제 정보, 멤버십 카드 정보 및 쿠폰 정보 중 적어도 하나를 포함하는 복수의 항목을 표시하는 터치스크린, 상기 터치스크린에 가해지는 터치 입력의 압력을 감지하는 압력 감지부, 및 상기 터치스크린과 상기 압력 감지부를 제어하는 제어부를 포함한다. 상기 제어부는, 상기 복수의 항목 중 어느 하나에 대한 제1 압력 이상의 제1 터치 입력이 감지되면, 상기 선택된 항목에 대응하는 결제 관련 정보를 활성화하고, 상기 선택된 항목에 대한 제2 입력이 수신되면, 상기 선택된 항목 또는 상기 선택된 항목에 포함된 코드 정보를 확대하여 표시하도록 제어한다. 이에 따라, 사용자는 시계형 이동 단말기에서 결제 카드, 멤버십 카드 및 쿠폰을 신속하게 선택하고, 선택된 항목을 확대 표시함으로써 결제 또는 인증 절차를 용이하게 수행할 수 있다.
